assumptions: Linearized schedule: modular additions replaced by XOR; low weights there are necessary, not sufficient, for low-weight real differences.
Exhaustive over message differences of weight 1 and 2 only (131,328 candidates).
Statistical tests: bit bias of W16..W63 and agreement of consecutive words, Bonferroni over all tests.
Bitcoin second header block: W0..W2 fixed per job, W3 = nonce, padding words constant. Outer block: W0..W7 = inner digest (varies per nonce), padding constant.
Timing comparisons are single-thread, release build, median of repeated batches; they are engineering measurements, not cryptographic results.
baseline: Verified cpu-backend scalar kernel: hoists W16, W17 and rounds 0..2 of the second header block; computes the outer schedule with the generic recurrence.
conclusion: NEGATIVE RESULT: no deviation from the baseline was detected in any tested configuration at the stated sample size and significance level. Linearized schedule: every 16-word window has GF(2) rank 512 (min over windows), so the expansion is invertible; requiring j words W16.. to vanish leaves null space dimension 512-32j (observed [480, 448, 416, 384, 352, 320, 288, 256, 224, 192, 160, 128, 96, 64, 32, 0]). Lowest linearized expanded weight (W16..W63) from a 1-bit message difference: 466 (bit 15); from 2-bit: 489 (bits 3, 291); longest run of zero expanded words from W16 among weight<=2 differences: 8. Real vs linearized schedule: agreement significantly above 1/2 last at W19. Real schedule statistics: 0 biased bits, consecutive-word correlations at []. Bitcoin header: second-block words independent of the nonce: [16,17]; the baseline already hoists W16, W17. Outer block: no word is digest-independent, 125 adds + 86 sigma evaluations per nonce are the minimum vs 144 + 96 naive. Measured (single thread, median of 7): generic outer schedule 118.25 ns, constant-folded 99.45 ns, difference 18.81 ns = 2.7% of one double compression (704.1 ns); folded variant identical to the generic one on all 1024 inputs.

dataset.description: n random messages from SplitMix64::stream(seed, i); timing on header-like blocks.

hypothesis: The SHA-256 message schedule has exploitable structure: low-weight linearized expanded differences, statistical dependence between expanded words, or nonce-independent work in Bitcoin header hashing beyond what the verified baseline kernel already precomputes.
methodology: Compute GF(2) ranks of schedule windows and null-space dimensions; enumerate weight-1/2 message differences through the linearized schedule; measure real-vs-linearized agreement and bit statistics on random messages; propagate nonce/digest dependence through the recurrence to count hoistable operations; time generic vs constant-folded outer schedule.
name: Structure and redundancy of the SHA-256 message schedule
null_hypothesis: Expanded words of random messages are unbiased and pairwise independent; all low-weight message differences expand to high-weight differences; the baseline already removes all nonce-independent schedule work.

outer_schedule_folding.note: timing is an engineering measurement and is excluded from the reproducibility digest

reproduction.method: full rerun with identical seed and parameters on a separate Rayon pool with a different thread count; SHA-256 of the canonical deterministic results compared

verification.method: GF(2) ranks recomputed on the transposed matrices; nonce/digest dependence of every expanded word checked against 64 concrete schedules with varying inputs
